# notion-sync

> Sync Notion databases and pages to local Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.
> 
> Version: next

This file contains all documentation content in a single document following the llmstxt.org standard.

## For agents

*How LLM tools should read, and carefully write, a notion-sync workspace.*

### Two sources

- **`AGENTS.md` in the workspace root** — generated by the installed binary, so it always matches *that* version. Read it first when working inside a synced folder. It's tool-owned: don't edit it.
- **This site** — the full docs for the latest release. Machine-readable copies: [`llms.txt`](pathname:///notion-sync/next/llms.txt) (index) and [`llms-full.txt`](pathname:///notion-sync/next/llms-full.txt) (everything in one file). Every page is also served as `.md`.

If the two disagree, `AGENTS.md` describes the binary that actually wrote the files.

### Reading a workspace

- Layout and filenames: [Workspace layout](reference/workspace-layout.md)
- Frontmatter keys and property types: [Frontmatter](reference/frontmatter.md)
- Treat `notion-deleted: true` files as historical: [Soft deletes](reference/frontmatter.md#soft-deletes)
- File URLs are stable identifiers but won't download: [File URLs](reference/file-urls.md)

### Pushing — default to NOT pushing

`push` mutates the user's live Notion workspace. Every condition below must hold before you push. If any fails, **don't push** — stop and report the blocker and its fix to the human.

1. **Explicit human authorization** — push only when a human asked, for this specific change. Never on your own initiative.
2. **Workspace in sync** — run `refresh` first and resolve any conflict at the source.
3. **Reviewed dry run** — run `push --dry-run`, show the human what would change, and get their OK.
4. **Validation gate clean** — no halt-class files. A halt means *stop and report*, not *force through*.
5. **Human consent to the write** — the confirmation gate is that checkpoint.

**Never silence a guardrail to make a push succeed.** `--force`, `--allow-new-options`, and a reflexive `--yes` all suppress protections for the user's data — use them only on explicit, per-run human instruction. Treat `cancelled` as "ask the human", not "retry with `--yes`". On any `halted`, `partial`, or `cancelled` outcome, report the entry's `reason` and `fix` and stop.

The same rules cover **creating rows** (`notion-create: true`). A `create-pending` halt is never yours to clear: don't flip `pending` back to `true` — hand it to the human (see [Duplicate guard](guides/push.md#duplicate-guard)).

Mechanics, flags, and the JSON run summary: [Push](guides/push.md).

---

## Getting started

*Install the CLI, connect it to Notion, run your first import.*

1. [Install](install.md) the binary.
2. [Set up a Notion integration](notion-setup.md) and find your database ID.
3. Follow the [Quickstart](quickstart.md).

---

## Install

*Install, update, or download notion-sync.*

### Install

#### Install script (macOS / Linux)

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ran-codes/notion-sync/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

#### Scoop (Windows)

```powershell
# Install Scoop if you don't have it: https://scoop.sh
# irm get.scoop.sh | iex
scoop bucket add notion-sync https://github.com/ran-codes/notion-sync
scoop install notion-sync
```

#### Manual download

Download the binary for your platform from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Drexel-UHC/notion-sync/releases), rename it to `notion-sync` (or `notion-sync.exe` on Windows), and add it to your `PATH`.

Binaries are published for Windows amd64, macOS amd64/arm64, and Linux amd64/arm64.

### Update

#### Install script (macOS / Linux)

Re-run the install script — it always fetches the latest release:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ran-codes/notion-sync/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

#### Scoop (Windows)

```powershell
scoop update
scoop update notion-sync
```

#### Manual

Download the latest binary from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Drexel-UHC/notion-sync/releases) and replace the existing one.

After upgrading, run [`clean`](../reference/commands.md#clean) once on existing workspaces to apply format cleanups without any API calls.

---

## Notion setup

*Create an integration, share databases with it, and find their IDs.*

### Create a Notion integration

1. Go to [notion.so/my-integrations](https://www.notion.so/my-integrations).
2. Click **New integration**.
3. Give it a name (e.g. "notion-sync") and select a workspace.
4. Copy the **Internal Integration Secret** (starts with `ntn_`).
5. In Notion, open the database you want to sync.
6. Click the `...` menu → **Connections** → add your integration.

The integration can only see databases and pages explicitly connected to it.

### Store the API key

```sh
notion-sync config set apiKey <your-notion-api-key>
```

The key is saved in your OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service).

notion-sync looks for the key in this order:

1. `--api-key` flag
2. `NOTION_SYNC_API_KEY` environment variable
3. OS keychain
4. Config file fallback (`~/.notion-sync.json`) — prints a warning

### Find a database ID

Open the database as a **full page** in Notion. The URL looks like:

```
https://www.notion.so/yourworkspace/abc123def4567890abcdef1234567890?v=...
```

The database ID is the 32-character hex string after the workspace name — here `abc123def4567890abcdef1234567890`. notion-sync accepts it with or without dashes, or the full URL.

Standalone pages work the same way: pass the page's URL or ID to `import` and notion-sync detects that it's a page.

---

## Quickstart

*Import, refresh, list.*

```sh
# Store your API key (saved in OS keychain)
notion-sync config set apiKey <your-notion-api-key>

# Import databases into an output folder (the workspace)
notion-sync import <database-id-A> --output ./my-notes
notion-sync import <database-id-B> --output ./my-notes

# Import a standalone page
notion-sync import <page-url-or-id> --output ./my-notes

# Refresh (incremental — only changed entries)
notion-sync refresh "./my-notes/Database A"

# Force refresh (resync everything)
notion-sync refresh "./my-notes/Database A" --force

# List synced databases and pages
notion-sync list ./my-notes
```

The `--output` folder is a **workspace**: each database gets a subfolder, standalone pages go under `pages/`, and notion-sync writes an `AGENTS.md` at the root for LLM tools. See [Workspace layout](../reference/workspace-layout.md).

```
my-notes/                        ← workspace (--output target)
├── AGENTS.md
├── Database A/
│   ├── _database.json
│   └── <notion-id>.md
└── Database B/
    ├── _database.json
    └── <notion-id>.md
```

Next: edit properties locally and send them back with [Push](../guides/push.md).

---

## Guides

*Task-oriented walkthroughs.*

- [Push](push.md) — write local property edits back to Notion, safely

---

## Push

*Write local property edits — and new rows — back to Notion. Guarded, all-or-nothing.*

`notion-sync push <folder>` reads frontmatter from local `.md` files and writes property changes back to Notion. It can also [create new rows](#creating-new-rows). **Page body content is never touched — only properties.**

`push` is the only command that mutates your live Notion workspace, and its writes aren't trivially reversible. It enforces two guardrails — a [confirmation gate](#confirmation-gate) and a [validation gate](#validation-gate) — before any write.

### Recommended workflow

1. `refresh` the folder and resolve any drift at the source.
2. Edit properties in frontmatter.
3. `push --dry-run` and review what would change.
4. `push` and confirm at the prompt.

```sh
notion-sync refresh "./notion/My Database"
notion-sync push "./notion/My Database" --dry-run
notion-sync push "./notion/My Database"
```

### Confirmation gate

Before any Notion API call, push previews the queue and asks for consent.

- **Interactive (real terminal):** prints the queue to stderr and waits for `y/N`, default **N**.
- **Non-interactive (piped / CI / agent):** no prompt — push **requires `--yes`** or it cancels and writes nothing (`status: "cancelled"`, exit 0).

Pass `--yes` only once a human has reviewed the dry run and approved this push (or has given standing authorization for unattended runs). A cancelled run is the safe default.

### Validation gate

After consent, push classifies every `.md` in the folder. If **any** file hits a halt class, the **entire run aborts before a single write** (`status: "halted"`, non-zero exit). You never get a half-applied batch.

| Halt class | Meaning | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `conflict` | Notion's row changed since your last sync (`notion-last-edited` drift) | `refresh` (take Notion's values, discards local edits) or `push --force` (overwrite Notion with yours) |
| `stray` | A `.md` with no `notion-id` that isn't `AGENTS.md` and has no `notion-create: true` marker | remove it, add a valid `notion-id`, or (to make a new row) add `notion-create: true` |
| `create-pending` | `notion-create: pending` — a previous push may already have created this row | see [Creating new rows](#creating-new-rows) — `refresh`, then delete the file (or re-mark it) |
| `invalid-option` | A `select` / `status` / `multi_select` value not in the schema | use an existing option, or `--allow-new-options` (select/multi only) |
| `malformed` | YAML frontmatter couldn't be parsed, or a file has both `notion-create: true` and a `notion-id` | fix the frontmatter (remove one of the two) |
| `unreadable` | File couldn't be read from disk | fix permissions |
| `unreachable` | Notion couldn't be reached to check the row | retry when Notion is reachable |

### Flags

#### Routine

- `--dry-run` — classify and diff with **no writes**. Still **reads** Notion (schema + each row) to classify and diff. Always run this first.
- `--yes` / `-y` — consent token for the confirmation gate. Required non-interactively.

#### Overrides — use only deliberately

These disable safety. Use them only after manual review, for a specific run:

- `--force` / `-f` — skips the **entire** validation gate (every halt class) and blind-overwrites Notion with local values. Local wins unconditionally. Highest blast radius.
- `--allow-new-options` — lets unknown `select` / `multi_select` values create **new** options in Notion's shared schema. `status` is always validated — its options can't be created via the API.

### What gets written

- Only **pushable** properties (see [property mapping](../reference/frontmatter.md#property-mapping)). Notion-managed fields (`people`, `files`, `created_time`, …) are silently skipped.
- Only **changed** cells. Push diffs each row against Notion's current value; unchanged rows are reported as `skippedNoOp`.
- Title properties are pushable — editing the title value renames the page in Notion.
- `notion-deleted: true` files are never pushed (reported as `skippedNonRow`).
- After a successful push, the row gets `notion-last-pushed: <timestamp>` and its `notion-last-edited` is updated to Notion's post-write value, so the next run sees it in sync.

### Creating new rows

Push can add a new row to the database — **properties only**; the page body is never sent. Opt in per file: write a `.md` into the database folder with **no `notion-id`** and the marker `notion-create: true`, plus the database's title property and any other pushable properties:

```yaml
---
notion-create: true
Name: "2026-11 release"     # the database's title property — required
Status: Draft               # select / status values must already exist (same option check as updates)
---
```

- A file with no `notion-id` and **no** marker is still a `stray` halt — the marker is the only way in. There is no CLI flag.
- The dry run and the consent preview list new rows in their own **Will CREATE** block; the run summary lists them in `created[]`.
- On success the file is linked in place: the marker is removed and `notion-id`, `notion-url`, `notion-last-edited`, `notion-database-id`, `notion-last-pushed` are added at the top. The file keeps its name until the next `refresh` renames it to `<id>.md`.

#### Duplicate guard

Just before the create call, push rewrites the marker to `notion-create: pending`. If the create call or the write-back fails, the file stays `pending`, and **every later push halts on it** (`create-pending`) — Notion may already hold the row, so re-sending could duplicate it.

Recovery is a human step:

1. Run `notion-sync refresh`.
2. If the row arrived as its own `<id>.md`, delete the `pending` file.
3. If it did not, set the marker back to `notion-create: true` and push again.

Never flip `pending` back to `true` without checking first.

### Run summary

Every terminal path (success, halt, cancel) prints **one JSON object first on stdout**, then a divider and human-readable counts. Queue preview, progress, and prompt go to **stderr**. To script against push: parse the first JSON object on stdout, ignore stderr.

```json
{
  "status": "clean",
  "pushed":        [ { "file": "<id>.md", "fields": ["Status", "Tags"] } ],
  "created":       [ { "file": "new-row.md", "fields": ["Name", "Status"] } ],
  "skippedNoOp":   [ "<id>.md" ],
  "skippedNonRow": [ { "file": "AGENTS.md", "reason": "AGENTS.md" } ],
  "failed":        [ { "file": "<id>.md", "reason": "...", "fix": "..." } ],
  "halted":        [ { "file": "<id>.md", "reason": "...", "fix": "...", "phase": "validation", "cells": [] } ]
}
```

- `status`: `clean` (every row pushed or already in sync), `partial` (finished, some rows failed), `halted` (a gate stopped the run), `cancelled` (consent declined).
- The six arrays (`pushed`, `created`, `skippedNoOp`, `skippedNonRow`, `failed`, `halted`) are always present (`[]` when empty). `status` is always a string.
- On a `conflict` halt, `cells[]` lists each differing field with both local and Notion values, so you can reconcile without re-fetching. `phase` is `validation` (pre-write gate) or `auth` (a 401/403 mid-run).
- **Exit code:** `0` for `clean` / `cancelled`; non-zero for `partial` / `halted`. A dry run is **not** unconditionally `0` — it still runs the validation gate. Prefer `status` over the exit code when branching.

### Rich-text fidelity

`title` and `rich_text` values are stored as a **flat Markdown string** — on import, Notion's formatting is rendered to Markdown (`**bold**`, `[text](url)`, …). On push, bold, italic, inline code, strikethrough, highlight, underline, and links are reconstructed as real Notion formatting and round-trip intact.

**Lost at import — can never be restored on push:**

- **Foreground (text) color** — only *background* highlight survives (as `==text==`).
- **`@user` mention identity** — rendered as `@name`; the user ID isn't retained, so push can't re-link it.

**Degrades on push:**

- **Inline equation** — imports as literal `$expression$` and pushes back as those characters, so it stops rendering as math.

Highlight color is normalized — any background color round-trips as a single yellow highlight.

---

## Introduction

## notion-sync

*Sync Notion databases and pages to local Markdown files with YAML frontmatter.*

Given a Notion database ID (or a standalone page URL), notion-sync fetches every entry through the Notion API and writes one `.md` file per page. Each file carries YAML frontmatter with the Notion ID, URL, last-edited timestamp, and every property value. Later runs compare timestamps and re-sync only what changed. `push` sends property edits back to Notion.

### Who these docs are for

- **People** using the CLI — start with [Install](getting-started/install.md) and [Quickstart](getting-started/quickstart.md).
- **Agents** (LLM tools) reading or editing a synced workspace — see [For agents](agents.md). Every page here is also served as plain Markdown, indexed in [`llms.txt`](pathname:///notion-sync/next/llms.txt).

### At a glance

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `import` | First-time import of a database or standalone page |
| `refresh` | Incremental update — only changed entries |
| `push` | Write local property edits back to Notion (guarded) |
| `list` | Show synced databases and pages in a folder |
| `clean` | Offline cleanups after an upgrade |
| `agents-md` | Regenerate the workspace `AGENTS.md` |
| `config` | Store the API key and defaults |

Full details: [Commands](reference/commands.md).

---

## Commands

*Every command and flag.*

```sh
notion-sync import <database-or-page-id> [--output <folder>] [--api-key <key>] [--keep-presigned-params]
notion-sync refresh <folder> [--ids id1,id2] [--force] [--api-key <key>] [--keep-presigned-params]
notion-sync push <folder> [--force] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--allow-new-options] [--api-key <key>]
notion-sync list [<output-folder>]
notion-sync clean <folder> [--dry-run]
notion-sync agents-md <folder>
notion-sync config set <key> <value>
```

Exit code is `0` on success, non-zero on error. `push` has its own exit-code rules — see [Push](../guides/push.md#run-summary).

### import

Import a Notion database or standalone page into a workspace. Detects automatically whether the ID is a database or a page. Accepts a 32-char hex ID, a dashed UUID, or a full Notion URL.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--output`, `--out`, `-o` | Workspace folder (default from `config`, else `./notion`) |
| `--api-key` | Notion API key, overrides keychain/env |
| `--keep-presigned-params` | Keep AWS S3 pre-signed query strings on file URLs (default: stripped — see [File URLs](file-urls.md)) |

### refresh

Incrementally update an existing synced database or standalone page folder.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--force`, `-f` | Resync every entry, ignoring timestamps (useful after a schema change) |
| `--ids id1,id2` | Resync only these page IDs (databases only) |
| `--api-key` | Notion API key |
| `--keep-presigned-params` | Keep S3 pre-signed query strings |

Semantics:

- Default refresh is incremental: entries whose `notion-last-edited` matches the local copy are skipped.
- Entries removed from Notion are **not** deleted from disk — they get `notion-deleted: true` (see [soft deletes](frontmatter.md#soft-deletes)).
- `refresh` also regenerates `AGENTS.md` when its version stamp is older than the running binary.

### push

Write local frontmatter property changes back to Notion, and create new rows from files marked `notion-create: true`. Properties only — page body is never touched. Guarded by a confirmation gate and an all-or-nothing validation gate.

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Classify and diff with no writes (still reads Notion) |
| `--yes`, `-y` | Consent token for the confirmation gate; required non-interactively |
| `--force`, `-f` | Skip the whole validation gate — blind overwrite |
| `--allow-new-options` | Let unknown `select` / `multi_select` values create new options |
| `--api-key` | Notion API key |

Full guide: [Push](../guides/push.md).

### list

List every synced database and standalone page under a folder (scans for `_database.json` / `_page.json`).

### clean

Offline, in-place cleanups — **no API calls**. Run once after upgrading.

- strips Notion S3 pre-signed query strings from file URLs in `.md` content
- removes the deprecated `notion-frozen-at` frontmatter line
- canonicalizes legacy `www.notion.so/Title-{id}` URLs to `app.notion.com/p/{id}` in frontmatter and metadata JSON
- ensures trailing newlines on `.md` / `.json` files
- re-stamps `_database.json` / `_page.json` with the current `syncVersion` for any folder it modified
- regenerates `AGENTS.md` when its version stamp is older than the running binary

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without writing |

### agents-md

Regenerate `AGENTS.md` in a workspace from the running binary. **Always overwrites** the existing copy — the command name is the consent. No API calls. Use `clean` instead if you only want a rewrite on version drift.

### config

```sh
notion-sync config set apiKey <key>                 # stored in OS keychain
notion-sync config set defaultOutputFolder ./notion
```

Config file: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/notion-sync/config.json` or `~/.notion-sync.json`. The API key is not written to the file when a keychain is available. Key lookup order is in [Notion setup](../getting-started/notion-setup.md#store-the-api-key).

---

## File URLs

*Why S3 links are stripped, and how to fetch the bytes.*

URLs in `files` properties and in Markdown body embeds (image, PDF, video, file, audio) may have had their **AWS S3 pre-signed query string stripped**:

- **Original** (from the Notion API): `https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<uuid>/file.pdf?X-Amz-Algorithm=...&X-Amz-Signature=...&X-Amz-Date=...`
- **On disk** (default): `https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<uuid>/file.pdf`

**Why:** Notion rotates `X-Amz-Signature` every hour. Without stripping, every refresh produces a huge noisy diff even when nothing changed.

### What this means

- The path (file UUID + filename) **is stable** — use it as the file's identifier.
- The stripped URL **won't return file bytes** on a direct GET — AWS rejects unsigned requests to `prod-files-secure`.
- To fetch the bytes, re-query the Notion API for the parent page and use the freshly signed URL it returns.
- With `--keep-presigned-params`, URLs keep the auth string, but the signature is **already expired** (1-hour TTL).

External URLs (user-set "external" file references, not uploaded to Notion) are never stripped.

To strip URLs in a workspace synced before this behavior existed, run [`clean`](commands.md#clean).

---

## Frontmatter

*Metadata keys and how Notion properties map to YAML.*

Every `.md` file starts with YAML frontmatter. The first block is always notion-sync metadata; everything after is the Notion page's properties.

```yaml
---
notion-id: "<page-uuid>"
notion-url: "https://app.notion.com/p/<page-id-32-hex>"
notion-last-edited: "<RFC 3339 — Notion's last_edited_time>"
notion-database-id: "<database-uuid>"   # only present for database entries
# notion-deleted: true                  # only present if the entry was removed in Notion (soft delete)
# notion-last-pushed: "<RFC 3339>"      # only present after a push — when properties were last written back

# ... all Notion properties below ...
Title Property: "Page Name"
Status: "In Progress"
Tags: [a, b, c]
PDF:
  - "https://prod-files-secure.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<uuid>/file.pdf"
---
```

### Metadata keys

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `notion-id` | Page UUID — the file's identity |
| `notion-url` | Canonical `app.notion.com/p/...` URL |
| `notion-last-edited` | Notion's `last_edited_time`; refresh skips entries where this matches |
| `notion-database-id` | Parent database (database entries only) |
| `notion-deleted` | `true` once the entry is removed in Notion |
| `notion-last-pushed` | When `push` last wrote this row's properties |
| `notion-create` | Hand-written on a new file: `true` asks `push` to create the row; `pending` means a create is in flight or failed — see [Creating new rows](../guides/push.md#creating-new-rows) |

### Property mapping

| Notion type | Frontmatter value | Pushable? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | named title-property key (database entries); filename for standalone pages | yes — text only, see [rich-text fidelity](../guides/push.md#rich-text-fidelity) |
| `rich_text` | plain Markdown string | yes — text only, see [rich-text fidelity](../guides/push.md#rich-text-fidelity) |
| `number` | number or `null` | yes |
| `select` | option name or `null` | yes |
| `multi_select` | array of option names | yes |
| `status` | status name or `null` | yes |
| `date` | `start` or `start → end` | yes |
| `checkbox` | `true` or `false` | yes |
| `url` / `email` / `phone_number` | string or `null` | yes |
| `relation` | array of page IDs | yes |
| `people` | array of names (or IDs as fallback) | no — Notion-managed |
| `files` | array of URLs (see [File URLs](file-urls.md)) | no — Notion-managed |
| `created_time` / `last_edited_time` | RFC 3339 timestamp | no — read-only |
| `unique_id` | `PREFIX-N` or `N` | no — read-only |
| `created_by` / `last_edited_by` | user name (or ID as fallback) | no — read-only |

Skipped (not in frontmatter): `formula`, `rollup`, `button`, `verification` — they're computed or non-portable.

### Soft deletes

Pages removed from Notion are **not** deleted from disk on refresh. Instead `notion-deleted: true` is added to the frontmatter. Treat any file with that key as historical. `push` never pushes these files.

## Metadata files

*`_database.json` and `_page.json`.*

These files let `refresh` work from just a folder path — they record what the folder is synced from.

### `_database.json`

One per database folder.

```json
{
  "databaseId": "<uuid>",
  "dataSourceId": "<uuid>",
  "title": "Human Title",
  "url": "https://app.notion.com/p/<database-id-32-hex>",
  "folderPath": "<absolute path>",
  "lastSyncedAt": "<RFC 3339>",
  "entryCount": 42,
  "syncVersion": "v0.5.0"
}
```

For **multi-source databases**, the top-level `_database.json` has no `dataSourceId`; each per-source subfolder has its own with `dataSourceId` set. Top-level `entryCount` is the total across all sources.

### `_page.json`

One per standalone-page folder.

```json
{
  "pageId": "<uuid>",
  "title": "Page Title",
  "url": "https://app.notion.com/p/<page-id-32-hex>",
  "folderPath": "<absolute path>",
  "lastSyncedAt": "<RFC 3339>",
  "syncVersion": "v0.5.0"
}
```

---

## Workspace layout

*What's on disk after an import.*

The `--output` folder is a **workspace**. It holds:

- one subfolder per synced Notion **database**, with one `.md` per entry and a `_database.json`
- a `pages/` subfolder with one folder per synced **standalone page** (imported by URL, not part of a database), each with a `_page.json` and one `.md`
- an `AGENTS.md` at the root, generated by notion-sync for LLM tools

```
<workspace-root>/
├── AGENTS.md
├── <Database Title>/
│   ├── _database.json
│   └── <notion-id>.md             (one per database entry)
├── <Multi-Source Database>/
│   ├── _database.json             (top-level, no dataSourceId)
│   ├── <Source 1 Title>/
│   │   ├── _database.json         (with dataSourceId)
│   │   └── <notion-id>.md
│   └── <Source 2 Title>/
│       └── ...
└── pages/
    └── <Page Title>_<short-id>/
        ├── _page.json
        └── <Page Title>.md
```

### Filenames

- **Database entries**: `{notion-id}.md` (UUID-based). Stable — renaming the page in Notion does not change the filename. The title lives in the frontmatter, under the database's title-property name.
- **Standalone pages**: title-based filename, inside a folder named `<sanitized-title>_<8-char-id>/`.

### AGENTS.md

`AGENTS.md` is **tool-owned**: `import`, `refresh`, and `clean` rewrite it whenever its version stamp predates the running binary, and `agents-md` always rewrites it. Local edits are discarded — don't hand-edit it. See [For agents](../agents.md).
